description_full:
"## Problem
question-quality.instructions.md line 16 already bans ambiguous pronouns, but only for interview questions. General agent chat responses still use \"this\", \"that\", \"the engine\" without establishing which entity is meant, making transcripts hard to follow without re-reading context.

## Goal
Author a new dedicated instructions file (e.g. .agents/instructions/orchestration/entity-disambiguation.instructions.md) defining a general-purpose protocol for all agent responses:
- First mention of an entity: full establishment (type, fully-qualified name/id, short summary or tags).
- Subsequent mentions within context proximity (same turn/recent turns): short id or name only is fine.
- Context reset (switching file/step/task): re-establish using the first-mention format.
- No bare pronoun references to entities ever.
Also update question-quality.instructions.md to reference/defer to the new file so the two are not duplicative, and update AGENTS.md's Clickable Reference Policy cross-reference if needed.

## Acceptance criteria
- New instructions file exists with the three-tier protocol (first mention / proximity / reset) and concrete examples.
- question-quality.instructions.md cross-references it instead of restating the general rule.
- Rule is scoped so agent modes beyond Interview Agent pick it up (verify applyTo/scope).

## Source
Derived from AGENT_WORKFLOW_OPTIMIZATIONS.md conversation, \"Step 3: Fixing Entity Ambiguity & Level of Detail\". User decision: create new dedicated file AND update question-quality.instructions.md.
"

  "---\ndescription: \"Use in every agent response, not only interview questions: the general entity disambiguation protocol. Covers first-mention establishment, proximity shorthand, context-reset re-establishment, and the ban on bare pronoun references to entities.\"\n---\n\n## Entity Disambiguation Protocol\n\nAmbiguous references (\"this\", \"that\", \"the engine\", \"it\") force the reader to reconstruct which entity is meant from surrounding context. This protocol applies to all agent responses — chat narration, status summaries, handoffs, and reviews — not only interview questions. Interview-specific reference formatting still lives in [question-quality.instructions.md](question-quality.instructions.md); link format itself is owned by the Clickable Reference Policy in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md).\n\n### The Three Tiers\n\n1. **First mention — full establishment.** The first time an entity appears in a response (or after a context reset, see below), state its type, its fully-qualified name or id, and a short summary or tag. Use a clickable reference per the Clickable Reference Policy where the entity has one (ticket, spec, doc, log).\n   - Example: \"Ticket [95403a71 Extend entity disambiguation protocol](.ticket/tickets/95403a71-cb2a-45ea-b48d-3444904e66dd/ticket.toml) (component agent-guidance, priority high) is open with no dependencies.\"\n2. **Proximity — short id or name only.** Within the same turn or the immediately following turns, while still discussing the same entity, a short id or name is sufficient. Do not re-establish type and summary every sentence.\n   - Example, continuing the same turn: \"95403a71 has no linked spec yet.\"\n3. **Context reset — re-establish.** When the conversation switches file, step, task, or subject, treat the next reference to a previously-mentioned entity as a first mention again: restate type, id, and summary before using shorthand.\n   - Example: after a detour into a different ticket or file, \"B [truncated]"

## Problem
A corpus-wide audit found ZERO files under `.agents/instructions/orchestration/**` declare `applyTo` frontmatter (~11+ files). Per `.agents/instructions/README.md`, omitting `applyTo` makes a file description-gated (surfaced on demand only); `applyTo: "**"` is the always-on form. Today every orchestration rule — general or narrow — is description-gated, so there is no way to guarantee a short set of general rules are always active while everything else stays scoped to relevant file domains.

## Scope (rescoped 2026-07-31, split out of the original ticket)
This ticket covers ONLY the near-term, hand-maintained, static convention:
- Define an `applyTo`-class scheme and apply it across `.agents/instructions/**`.
- A small set of SHORT, GENERAL orchestration rules get `applyTo: "**"` (always-on, corpus-wide). These must stay short and general — not a dumping ground for domain specifics.
- All other guidance files become specialized per file domain via domain-scoped `applyTo` globs (e.g. `**/*.md`, `**/*.toml`, `**/*.json`, `**/*.rs`) instead of being left purely description-gated.
- Includes fixing `.agents/instructions/orchestration/entity-disambiguation.instructions.md` specifically — this is what satisfies ticket 95403a71's reopened acceptance criterion 3 (verify the rule is scoped so agent modes beyond Interview Agent pick it up).

## Explicitly out of scope
- Any new frontmatter key beyond `applyTo` (no tags, no priority weights, no custom scoping keys).
- Any runtime/tooling-driven dynamic selection (e.g. selecting guidance by ticket domain tag at dispatch time). That is deferred to a separate future ticket that depends on rule-api deployment.

## Acceptance criteria
- A written `applyTo`-class convention exists (e.g. as a section in `.agents/instructions/README.md` or equivalent) naming: which files qualify for `applyTo: "**"`, and the domain-glob pattern used for specialized files.
- Every file under `.agents/instructions/orchestration/**` has non-empty `applyTo` frontmatter: either `"**"` for the always-on general set, or a domain-scoped glob for specialized files. Verify with a repo-wide grep confirming no file in that directory is missing `applyTo`.
- `.agents/instructions/orchestration/entity-disambiguation.instructions.md` specifically has `applyTo` frontmatter set (not `"**"` unless it qualifies as short/general per the convention above), closing ticket 95403a71's acceptance criterion 3.
- No file touched by this ticket gains any frontmatter key other than `applyTo`.

## Source
Split out of the original "Scoped/dynamic guidance injection by ticket domain tag" ticket during a scoping interview on 2026-07-31. The interview resolved the ambiguity between static, hand-maintained `applyTo` classing (this ticket) and a future runtime/tag-driven injection mechanism (moved to a new deferred ticket, linked non-blocking).

turns.content:
## Verdict

This spec is not promotable as-is. It reads like a design memo that borrowed "Acceptance Criteria" and "Open Questions" headers to look rigorous — three tickets already shipped instruction files that quote it as authoritative, yet the spec's own AC only requires that *the document contain certain sections*, not that any behavior be true or checkable. Zero validation executions are recorded against it (`mcp_test-mcp_test_list_executions` for ticket 1a240fdc returns `{"count":0}`), and the spec never says so. Six Open Questions are still live, including whether the core "immutable plan" claim can even be enforced — that's a draft honestly admitting it isn't done, then getting cited as settled ground by downstream instructions anyway.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Location | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | high | [body.md](.spec/specs/1b654f30-d1a4-4cb4-ab2e-8355dfe5a758/body.md#L126-L131) | Acceptance Criteria are self-referential document-content checks ("This spec defines...", "This spec includes...", "This spec explicitly reconciles..."). None assert a checkable system property; all three are satisfied by the document existing. Not "mechanically checkable" in any sense beyond `grep`. | Rewrite as criteria about the *system*: e.g. "a validator can parse the plan JSON schema and reject a plan missing a required field" — and cite the validator, once it exists. |
| 2 | high | whole document | Zero occurrences of an executable command, test file, or CI job anywhere in body.md. `validation_commands` in the Plan Schema (L58-95) is a placeholder type string, never an example. Search for "cargo test", "playwright", "e2e" in this file: none. | Add a Validation section naming what currently validates this spec (nothing) and what will (validator ticket, schema linter), or state explicitly "no executable validation exists for this spec at draft time." |
| 3 | high | [body.md](.spec/specs/1b654f30-d1a4-4cb4-ab2e-8355dfe5a758/body.md#L132-L139) (Open Questions 1-6) | Six unresolved questions, including Q3: "nothing described here mechanically prevents a Worker from improvising beyond its step." That's the load-bearing claim of the whole spec (Worker boundary), stated as unenforced. Yet AC #1 (L127) already claims the boundary is "defined" — defined ≠ enforced, and the spec conflates the two. | Split AC #1 into "boundary documented" (done) vs. a separate, blocked-on-Q3 criterion for enforcement. Don't let downstream tickets cite the boundary as if Q3 is resolved. |
| 4 | med | [body.md](.spec/specs/1b654f30-d1a4-4cb4-ab2e-8355dfe5a758/body.md#L60) | "Concrete JSON schema sketch" — concrete and sketch directly contradict each other in the same sentence. It's markdown-embedded JSON with English-language field descriptions (`"string (verifiable condition, e.g. ...)"`), not an actual schema (no JSON Schema / TypeScript type / serde struct). No validator could consume this without a human rewriting it. | Either ship an actual `.schema.json` / Rust struct as a code_ref, or rename the section "Illustrative Plan Shape" and stop calling it concrete. |
| 5 | med | [body.md](.spec/specs/1b654f30-d1a4-4cb4-ab2e-8355dfe5a758/body.md#L8-L14) | Problem section is pure narrative justification ("Dilutes instructions," "Adds structural token overhead," "Offsets the cheap tier's savings") — argues *why* the reader should care, states no contract. | Compress L8-14 to 2 lines: "Multi-hop delegation (T0→T1/T2→T3) adds a spawn, a context-bundle re-inflation, and a retry-escalation hop per level; see shared-context-bundle.instructions.md for measured duplicate-read costs." Est. save: ~5 lines. |
| 6 | med | [body.md](.spec/specs/1b654f30-d1a4-4cb4-ab2e-8355dfe5a758/body.md#L96-L111) | "What Changes / What Is Preserved" narrates rationale per bullet ("today this is described as an ongoing orchestrator activity across the session. Under the two-tier model it becomes...") instead of stating the delta as a table (old rule → new rule → status). | Convert to a 3-column table: Rule / Old / New. Est. save: ~6-8 lines, and it becomes scannable. |
| 7 | low | [body.md](.spec/specs/1b654f30-d1a4-4cb4-ab2e-8355dfe5a758/body.md#L42) | Worker tier is stated as "T2 default... droppable to T3 per-step" — no contract for *who decides* the drop, or what signal triggers it. Prose, not a rule. | State the decision rule explicitly (what signal → drop to T3) or flag as an Open Question instead of asserting it as settled. |
| 8 | low | [body.md](.spec/specs/1b654f30-d1a4-4cb4-ab2e-8355dfe5a758/body.md#L44) `return_contract.shape` | `"shape": "string (e.g. \"diff_summary \| validation_result \| blocker\")"` is a comment, not an enum. A dispatcher parsing this plan has no closed set of valid shapes to switch on. | Define `shape` as an actual enum with per-shape required_fields, not one shared field list. |

## Cut List (narration bloat)

- **L8-14** (Problem section, 3 bullets) → compress to 2 lines. **Save ~5 lines.**
- **L96-111** (What Changes / What Is Preserved, prose form) → convert to table. **Save ~6-8 lines.**
- **L26-29** (Non-Goals) has three lines of cross-spec attribution prose ("owned by a4d61b8c... owned by model-prices.instructions.md...") that could be a one-line "see Related Specs" pointer since Related Specs (L120-124) already restates the same ownership. **Save ~2-3 lines of duplication.**

Total realistic savings: **~13-16 lines** out of 139 (~10%) — not huge, but this a small spec; the ratio of "explains why" to "states what" is still worse than it should be for something citing itself as normative to three shipped instruction files.

## Missing Contracts

- A closed enum for `return_contract.shape` with per-variant `required_fields`, not a shared string list.
- A machine-checkable form of `done_criteria` (currently free-text like `"cargo test -p session-api passes"` — fine as an example, but no schema requires it be an actual runnable command vs. a vague English sentence).
- An explicit invariant for `depends_on` (acyclic? forward-only by `step_id` ordering? unspecified).
- A structural enforcement mechanism for `target_path` scope-limiting (Open Question 3 admits none exists) — must be either specified or explicitly deferred with an owning ticket, not left as a rhetorical question.
- A plan versioning/amendment contract (Open Question 6) — without it, "immutable: true" is unfalsifiable.

## Validation Gaps

- **No executable validation exists for this spec's own claims.** Confirmed: `mcp_test-mcp_test_list_executions` for ticket 1a240fdc returns zero executions. The spec never states this gap — it's silently omitted, which is exactly the failure mode flagged in the brief.
- The Plan Schema (L58-95) has no accompanying validator, test fixture, or example plan instance anywhere in the repo referenced by code_refs.
- Acceptance Criteria (L126-131) require no test, no command, no CI gate — they're satisfied by prose existing.

## Drift (spec vs. shipped instruction files)

No hard contradictions found, but two soft drifts:

1. **retry-limit.instructions.md** presents "one self-fix retry, then escalate" as a firm, load-bearing rule resolving "Open Question 2." The spec (L133-135) still lists Q2 as literally unresolved ("does the whole Plan invalidate... or can the Step be patched in place?... is unresolved"). The instruction file answers a question the spec claims is still open — draft-state spec, but downstream already treats it as settled. This is a state-machine problem: promote the spec or mark Q2 resolved-by-reference to retry-limit.instructions.md.
2. **split-responsibility-testing.instructions.md** cites "spec 1b654f30, Worker capability boundary table" as authorizing the frontier/worker test-authoring split — but that table (L48-56) says nothing about *test file authorship* specifically; the instruction file extrapolates a new rule ("Worker may not edit test files") not present in the cited table. Not contradictory, but it's a citation overreach: the spec is being used as authority for a rule it doesn't actually state.

## Promote Recommendation

**needs-rewrite** — not promote-after-listed-fixes. The AC rewrite (finding #1) and validation-gap disclosure (finding #2) aren't line edits, they require redefining what "acceptance criteria" means for this document before it leaves draft, and Q2/Q3/Q6 need explicit resolved-or-deferred status given that instruction files are already citing this spec as settled.

arguments.description:
## Problem

This session originally assumed a read-index staleness defect in ticket-api as a premise for spec ticket 54114fc9 (deterministic Rust execution controller). Research could not reproduce a staleness defect in the read-index itself: `memory-api/crates/ticket-api/src/storage/store/scan_helpers.rs::entry_is_current` (L176-214) correctly detects on-disk/index `type` mismatches, and `integrate_entry` overwrites stale entries correctly, with a passing regression suite.

The more likely root cause is workspace/root RESOLUTION picking a different `.ticket` store than the one actually reconciled — not index staleness per se. This matches the symptom already reported in ticket 1d6a033e: `add_edge` fails with entity-not-found on entities that `get_ticket`/`update_ticket` resolve successfully moments earlier against the same explicit workspace path, suggesting `add_edge` resolves entities through a different (stale or narrower-scoped) index/lookup path than other ticket-mcp handlers.

## Goal

Investigate and confirm (or rule out) the actual root cause: workspace/root resolution divergence between ticket-mcp handlers (e.g. `add_edge` vs. `get_ticket`/`update_ticket`), rather than assuming an unproven read-index staleness defect. Reconcile findings with 1d6a033e, which may be the same underlying bug or a duplicate.

## Acceptance criteria
- Root cause is confirmed with reproduction steps (not assumed), covering the divergence between `add_edge` and other ticket-mcp handlers on workspace/root resolution.
- Relationship to 1d6a033e is stated explicitly: same bug, duplicate, or genuinely distinct.
- No downstream spec (including 54114fc9) is left assuming an unconfirmed root cause for this class of failure.

## Source
Split out of ticket 54114fc9 per interview decision (2026-07-31, Q6): "Split a separate investigation ticket for the unreproduced staleness bug (suspected workspace/root resolution, cf. 1d6a033e) rather than letting the spec assume a root cause" — answered yes.

I stopped immediately once I noticed and did not touch that path further. New untracked files in that directory (shadow.rs, supervisor.rs, watcher.rs, tests/*) were untouched and are still present. **Please check whether the owning agent/session for mcp-toolmon can redo that work**, or check editor local history for a snapshot.

- Test added: `session_record_persists_and_loads_handoff_id_lists` in [store_tests/finish/handoff_lifecycle.rs](memory-api/crates/session-api/src/store_tests/finish/handoff_lifecycle.rs) — persists via `SessionStorePlan::persist()`, reloads via `read_session`, asserts both lists survive.

Both new `Vec<String>` fields use `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]` on `SessionRecord` and `PersistedSessionManifest` — legacy JSON missing these keys deserializes to empty vecs, and records with empty vecs re-serialize without emitting the keys (matches the `track_id`/`parent_session_id` precedent). `SessionHandoffRecord.target_session_id` is `Option`, defaulting to `None` for legacy handoff records (deserializes as unclaimed/backlog-visible, which is the correct legacy interpretation).
